title: Client-Side Routing: React Router and Next.js Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on client-side routing: the mental model, React Router routes, nested routes and outlets, params and search params, navigation, loaders, and how Next.js file-system routing compares.

chapters.title: Client-Side Routing Mental Model
points: Client-side routing: JS intercepts link clicks, updates the URL with the History API (pushState), and re-renders the matching UI without a full page reload
Router = URL to UI map: on every location change the router matches the path against route definitions and renders the matched element
Back/forward fire a popstate event; the router listens and re-matches, so history entries stay in sync with the UI
Server must return index.html for every unknown path (SPA fallback), otherwise refreshing /users/42 gives a 404
Plain <a href> triggers a full reload and loses app state; use <Link> or <NavLink> for in-app navigation

chapters.title: React Router Routes and Nested Outlets
points: createBrowserRouter([{ path, element, children }]) plus <RouterProvider router={router} /> declares the route tree as data
Nested routes: child path is relative to the parent and the child renders inside the parent's layout
The parent renders <Outlet /> where the matched child appears; no Outlet means children never show
Index route ({ index: true }) renders at the parent's exact path; a layout route with no path only adds shared UI
Path matching ranks by specificity, not order: static beats dynamic (:id) beats splat (*); path: '*' is the catch-all 404 route

chapters.title: URL Params and Search Params
points: Path params: path '/users/:id' and useParams() returns { id } as a string, so convert with Number() before comparing or using it
Search params: const [sp, setSp] = useSearchParams(); sp.get('q') returns string or null; setSp({ q: 'abc' }) updates the URL
Use path params to identify a resource (/users/42) and search params for optional state like filter, sort and page
Search params live in the URL so they survive refresh and are shareable; replacing the whole object drops the other keys
Optional segments are supported with a trailing ? (/:lang?/about); params from parent routes are merged into useParams in children

chapters.title: Navigation and Loaders
points: <Link to> for clicks, <NavLink> adds an active class and isActive state, and useNavigate() navigates imperatively after an action
navigate(-1) goes back; navigate('/x', { replace: true }) swaps the history entry, which suits redirects after login
<Navigate to='/login' replace /> redirects declaratively during render, such as in a protected route guard
A loader on a route fetches data before render and the component reads it with useLoaderData(), avoiding fetch-in-useEffect waterfalls
Loaders for sibling and nested routes run in parallel; an action handles form submits and revalidates loaders afterward; throw a Response or error to reach errorElement

chapters.title: Next.js Framework Routing
points: App Router is file-system based: a folder under app/ is a route segment and page.tsx makes it publicly reachable
layout.tsx wraps child segments, persists across navigation without remounting, and is the Next.js equivalent of an Outlet layout
Dynamic segments: [id] gives params.id, [...slug] is catch-all, and [[...slug]] is optional catch-all; params is a Promise in newer versions, so await it
Navigate with next/link <Link> (prefetches visible links) and, in client components, useRouter().push from next/navigation, not next/router

loading.tsx wraps the segment in Suspense and error.tsx wraps it in an error boundary; not-found.tsx renders for notFound() in its segment, and only the root app/not-found.tsx also handles unmatched URLs; searchParams are a page prop, and useSearchParams needs a client component

chapters.title: Routing Cheat Sheet
points: React Router: createBrowserRouter, RouterProvider, children, Outlet, index: true, path '*'
Hooks: useParams (path), useSearchParams (query), useNavigate (imperative), useLoaderData (route data), useLocation
Components: Link, NavLink (active state), Navigate (redirect on render), Outlet (child slot)
Next.js: app/users/[id]/page.tsx, layout.tsx, loading.tsx, error.tsx, not-found.tsx, next/link, next/navigation
Rules: params are strings, replace for redirects, SPA needs server fallback, loaders beat useEffect fetching
